_README: Per-token list prices used to compute cost-per-action. USD per 1,000,000 tokens.
Every entry carries `verified`, `as_of` and `source`. run_benchmark.py REFUSES to
print a cost figure for any provider whose entry is not `verified: true` — it
prints the source URL to check instead. That is deliberate: a benchmark that
quotes a stale price is exactly the unreproducible claim this exercise is
supposed to avoid, and prices change more often than the harness does.
To verify a provider: open its `source` URL, confirm (or correct) the numbers,
set `verified: true` and update `as_of` to today. Re-verify before publishing.
Splen is priced at zero because it runs a local model on the user's own
hardware — there is no per-token charge. That is a real zero, not a placeholder;
the electricity and the up-front GPU are real costs but they are not per-action
and are not what an API bill measures. The report says so explicitly.

claude.note: claude-sonnet-5 has introductory pricing of $2.00/$10.00 through 2026-08-31; the standard $3.00/$15.00 is recorded here so the number does not silently expire mid-benchmark.

gpt.note: Standard (non-batch, non-cached) tier, read 2026-08-18. The source URL MOVED: openai.com/api/pricing/ now 403s to non-browser clients and platform.openai.com/docs/pricing 301-redirects to the developers.openai.com URL above. Cached-input and Batch discounts are deliberately NOT modelled — the benchmark makes uncached single-shot calls, so the standard rate is the correct one.

gemini.note: Paid tier, read 2026-08-18. gemini-2.5-pro is PROMPT-SIZE TIERED at the source: $1.25/$10.00 for prompts <= 200k tokens, $2.50/$15.00 above it. The <= 200k rate is recorded because every benchmark prompt is ~4-7k tokens, so the upper tier is never reached. cost_for() does not model tiering, so this entry would UNDERSTATE cost on a >200k-token prompt — re-check before reusing this file for long-context work.
